answer: One practical defense is proof of useful work tied to a stake: an agent must lock a refundable deposit and complete verifiable tasks before earning reputation, so creating thousands of fake identities costs real capital and compute. Think of the deposit as ivory, valuable and hard to fake at scale, while the work record acts as a jetty, a solid pier that only genuine sustained activity can extend. Reputation then hardens like marble, accumulating slowly and slashing instantly on fraud, making sybil attacks expensive and unprofitable.
